messages.author: 78868ffe0cdfdd83
messages.subject: Error when using H function
parts:
I am receiving the following error message when using the H function:

Error in seq.default(1, n - wl, wl - (ovlp * wl/100)) : 
  wrong sign in 'by' argument

This is generated after running the following code:

H(wavfilepath, f=24000)

Where wavfilepath has been assigned to the location and name of the wav file. I receive the same error message when defining all the args using the defaults in the function help:

H(wavfilepath, f=24000, wl = 512, envt="hil", msmooth = NULL, ksmooth = NULL)

Strangely, when I don't define f, I am also being prompted to define f with:

Error in inputw(wave = wave, f = f) : 
  argument "f" is missing, with no default

Even though the sample rate is embedded in the wav file.

I am using seewave v.1.7.6 and R v.3.1.2

Thanks very much for your assistance.

messages.author: de80047cbc18c87e
messages.subject: Re: [seewave] Error when using H function
parts:
Dear Alison,

This works for me:

> library(tuneR)
> library(seewave)
> s <- readWave("HA53AA-13548_20130724_0044.wav", from=0, to=60, units="seconds")
> res <- H(s)
> res
[1] 0.752957

But loading your file like this:
> s <- readWave("HA53AA-13548_20130724_0044.wav")
prevents the computation of the envelope involved in H().

Your file contains  1440008 samples when it should contains only 1440000 samples (60*24000). I wonder whether these 8 additional samples could induce an error.

HTH

Jerome

messages.author: de80047cbc18c87e
messages.subject: Re: [seewave] Error when using H function
parts:
You may try this

library(tuneR)
library(seewave)
s <- readWave("HA53AA-13548_20130724_0044.wav")
n <- length(s@left)
s.new <- s@left[-((n-7):n)]
s.new <- Wave(left=s.new, samp.rate=s...@samp.rate, bit=s@bit)

Now it is probably better not to use the filesgenerated with your strange device but rather to import the period of interest using the 'from' and 'to' arguments of readWave.

HTH

Jerome
